name: Orvana Bioluminescent Hem Formal Gown
description:
Orvana's signature formal gown uses a TESSERA-licensed bioluminescent thread woven into the hem and train — living filaments that emit a slow, pulsing light in blue-white or amber tones, sustained by body heat and requiring no external power source. The gown itself is cut in heavy silk-analog with a fluid column silhouette, structured at the bodice with internal boning and a chromatic lining that catches the bioluminescent light and redistributes it upward through the fabric in a subtle gradient. A deep rear vent accommodates geneware tail modifications up to standard C-class length, and the back closure is a magnetic press-seam that adjusts automatically to wing-brace hardware or scapular augment housings.

At Tier 3-4 pricing, the Orvana gown is aspirational for the professional class and practical for the lower corporate tier. It is frequently worn to Ringo-affiliated media events, TESSERA client galas, and mid-level corponation award ceremonies. The bioluminescent hem dims after approximately 300 hours of activation and cannot be recharged — owners either resell or relegate the gown to non-luminescent occasions, which it handles with grace.
cultural_context: The Orvana gown marks a specific stratum of Meridian social life: people who have made it far enough to attend events with bioluminescent dress codes but are still calculating whether the purchase is worth the month it costs. TESSERA's licensing of bioluminescent thread to fashion labels has made living-light fabric accessible below Spire pricing, which has complicated what was once an exclusive status signal.
story_hooks: The bioluminescent thread in a batch of Orvana gowns is dimming prematurely — TESSERA's licensing division is quietly investigating whether a competitor has introduced a biological inhibitor into Orvana's supply chain.
A character attends a corponation event in this gown, and the pulsing hem syncs unexpectedly with a nearby BCI broadcast — drawing attention they cannot afford.
A Tier 2 tailor acquires a damaged Orvana gown and carefully harvests the still-active bioluminescent thread for resale, piece by piece.

physical_description.visual_profile: A floor-length column gown with ethereal presence. The silhouette is elegantly restrained—fitted through the torso, flowing from hip to ankle with a dramatic rear train. The hem and train edges glow with soft, pulsing bioluminescent threads in blue-white or amber, creating a living halo of light that shifts with body heat. The overall effect is both ethereal and deliberately engineered.
physical_description.fit: Structured column silhouette. Fitted bodice with internal boning for support, tapering to a fluid, relaxed drape from hip to floor. Accommodates geneware tails (up to C-class length) and scapular/wing-brace augmentation housings through a deep rear vent and adjustable magnetic back closure.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy silk-analog (synth-silk blend), chromatic lining that refracts bioluminescent light upward through the weave
physical_description.texture: Smooth, lustrous face with subtle drape weight; bioluminescent hem threads create fine, almost imperceptible texture variation along edges. Internal boning structure creates subtle ribbing at the bodice when fitted.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep jewel-tone base (sapphire, emerald, or burgundy typical), with a chromatic gradient lining visible at the rear vent. The bioluminescent hem glows blue-white or warm amber—color is user-configurable or batch-specific at purchase.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic press-seam back closure that auto-adjusts for augment hardware. No visible fasteners; seamless integration with cybernetic modifications.
distinctive_features: TESSERA-licensed bioluminescent thread woven into hem and 2-meter train
Living filaments powered by body heat only—no external power required
Chromatic lining redirects bioluminescent glow upward through main fabric in subtle gradient
Deep rear vent (12-15cm) accommodates tail and wing-brace hardware
Adjustable magnetic closure for scapular augment housings
Pulsing light effect synchronized with wearer's core temperature (slower when cool, brighter when active)
Orvana couture branding (subtle woven label at back seam)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 aspirational luxury. Entry-level formal wear for professional class and lower corporate tier. Costs approximately one month's salary for Tier 3 wage earner.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals upward mobility and corporate event access. Worn by TESSERA clients, mid-level corponation employees, and Ringo-affiliated media professionals. The bioluminescent hem is a status flex that is slowly being democratized—expensive enough to signal success, accessible enough that it's no longer purely Spire-exclusive. Wearing one says: 'I attend events that matter, and I can afford the living light.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new; bioluminescent threads dim after ~300 hours of activation and cannot be recharged. After deactivation, the gown remains elegant non-luminescent formal wear, though some owners relegate faded dresses to secondary events or resale market. Well-maintained examples show minimal wear to bodice; trains may show light creasing or subtle scuffing from movement.

image_prompt: A striking bioluminescent gown on a dark-skinned model with subtle chromatic augmentation around the eyes, shot in moody studio lighting. The gown is a deep sapphire silk-analog column silhouette, fitted bodice with internal structure visible as subtle ribbing, flowing train trailing behind. The hem and train edges glow with soft blue-white bioluminescent threads pulsing gently, casting light upward through the fabric in ethereal gradient waves. The rear vent is visible, showing the chromatic lining catching and refracting the bioluminescent glow. Background is dark urban—floor of brushed steel or wet pavement reflecting the hem's light. The model stands in three-quarter pose, one hand at her side, the other lifted slightly, allowing the train to pool dramatically. Ambient light is cool and moody; the gown's glow is the primary light source on the fabric itself. Ultra-high detail on the glowing threads and the way light propagates upward through the silk. Cyberpunk formal elegance. --ar 2:3 --v 6
